annotation.authors_or_issuer: Frey, C.B.; Osborne, M.A.; Holmes, C.; Rahbari, E.; Curmi, E.; Garlick, R. et al. (Citi GPS / Oxford Martin School)
key_provisions_or_claims: 47% of US jobs at high risk of automation, with wide variation across countries (e.g., 85% Ethiopia, 35% UK per World Bank) and cities.
Perception/manipulation, creative and social intelligence remain bottlenecks to automation.
Robot payback periods are falling, accelerating adoption.
Recommends education investment, active labour market policies, and job-creation policies in cities.
Includes a section on whether robot laws on privacy, ethics and liability will slow change.
annotation.summary_en: Citi GPS and Oxford Martin School report assessing the susceptibility of jobs, countries and cities to automation, sector impacts, productivity and inflation effects, and policy responses such as education and job-creation measures. It includes a section on robot laws (privacy, ethics, liability). The collector title mismatches the content.
annotation.title_clean: Technology at Work v2.0: The Future Is Not What It Used to Be
